content.user_title: Stabilize Async Tests with Condition Waiting
content.value_statement: Flaky tests often fail because they guess how long async work takes. This skill shows Claude, Codex, and Claude Code how to wait for real conditions instead of fixed delays.
actual_capabilities: Explains when arbitrary sleeps in tests should be replaced with condition polling.
Provides a reusable waitFor pattern with timeout handling and polling intervals.
Shows event-based helpers for waiting on event type, event count, or custom predicates.
Identifies cases where a fixed timeout is still valid for timing behavior tests.
Documents common waiting mistakes such as stale state, missing timeouts, and over-fast polling.
limitations: Does not run or modify tests automatically without user direction.
Requires the project to expose observable state, events, or files that can be polled.
Does not replace timing assertions for debounce, throttle, or interval behavior.
Example helpers reference a specific ThreadManager style and may need adaptation.

use_cases.title: Fix flaky CI tests
use_cases.description: Replace sleep-based waits with condition checks that pass under different machine speeds and loads.

use_cases.title: Improve async integration tests
use_cases.description: Wait for events, state changes, or result counts before making assertions in asynchronous workflows.

use_cases.title: Review test reliability patterns
use_cases.description: Find timing guesses and decide whether to poll for state or document a real timing requirement.

prompt_templates.title: Find fixed sleeps
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a flaky test file
prompt_templates.prompt: Use condition-based-waiting to review this test file for setTimeout, sleep, or fixed delay patterns. Explain which waits should become condition checks.

prompt_templates.title: Rewrite one flaky wait
prompt_templates.prompt: Use condition-based-waiting to replace this arbitrary delay with a waitFor condition. Keep the test intent the same and include a clear timeout message.

prompt_templates.title: Design event wait helpers
prompt_templates.prompt: Use condition-based-waiting to design helper functions for waiting on event type, event count, and event predicates in this test suite.

prompt_templates.title: Audit timing exceptions
prompt_templates.prompt: Use condition-based-waiting to audit these tests. Separate true timing behavior tests from flaky timing guesses, and recommend the smallest safe changes.

output_examples.input: A test waits 300 milliseconds before checking whether two tool calls started.
output_examples.output: The skill would recommend waiting until two matching tool call events are observed, then asserting on the result.

output_examples.input: A test checks a result after a short delay and sometimes fails in CI.
output_examples.output: The skill would suggest polling for the result to become available with a timeout and a descriptive failure message.

output_examples.input: A debounce test waits for a documented interval before asserting behavior.
output_examples.output: The skill would keep the timed wait if the delay is part of the behavior under test and the reason is documented.

best_practices: Wait for the specific state, event, count, or file condition that proves readiness.
Always include a timeout with an error message that names the condition being awaited.
Poll fresh state inside the loop instead of caching values before the wait begins.
anti_patterns: Do not add arbitrary sleeps because a test sometimes fails in CI.
Do not poll every millisecond unless the timing requirement is justified.
Do not use condition waiting for tests that are explicitly about timing intervals.

faq.question: What problem does this skill solve?
faq.answer: It helps remove flaky waits from tests by replacing fixed delays with checks for real conditions.

faq.question: Can I still use setTimeout in tests?
faq.answer: Yes, when the test verifies real timing behavior. The skill recommends documenting why the timeout is required.

faq.question: What should a wait condition check?
faq.answer: It should check the observable result you need, such as an event, state value, count, or file existence.

faq.question: How long should the polling interval be?
faq.answer: The examples use 10 milliseconds as a practical default that avoids excessive CPU use.

faq.question: Does this skill include runnable utilities?
faq.answer: It includes TypeScript example helpers that can be adapted to a project test suite.

faq.question: Is this skill specific to Claude Code?
faq.answer: No. It is written for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows that improve test reliability.
